one_line_reason: A few single-ingredient human RCTs of oregano essential oil or extract exist, with mixed results (one positive lipid signal, one null antioxidant/lipid signal, one positive but low-certainty symptom signal in a clinical population).

selected.intervention: Origanum vulgare subsp. hirtum essential oil (oral), 14-day intervention, vs control (also compared against Origanum dubium and Lavandula angustifolia oils)
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (essential oil intervention duration given as 14 days, no mg/mL dose stated in abstract)
selected.why_selected: Single-ingredient (true oregano subspecies) RCT in a general athletic population with a statistically significant favorable HDL-C change

selected.intervention: Origanum vulgare (oregano) extract delivered via fortified juice, 300 mg/day or 600 mg/day total phenolic compounds, oral, 4 weeks vs placebo juice
selected.dose_as_stated: 300 mg/day or 600 mg/day (as total phenolic compounds from oregano extract)
selected.primary_outcome: serum lipids and biomarkers of lipid peroxidation
selected.why_selected: Clean single-ingredient, dose-stated RCT in healthy volunteers on the antioxidant claim oregano is often marketed for; found increased phenolic excretion but no significant effect on lipids or lipid peroxidation

selected.population: patients with chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps (CRSsNP), within a network meta-analysis of 47 RCTs across 18 herbal medicines
selected.intervention: Origanum vulgare (herbal preparation, specific form/dose not given in this review-level abstract)
selected.primary_outcome: symptom improvement and health-related quality of life
selected.why_selected: Identified within a network meta-analysis as the most beneficial single herbal treatment for this specific rhinosinusitis subtype, though rated low certainty of evidence

blockers: 34496170 and 34496170-type essential-oil dosing (mL or drops) may not map cleanly to a capsule/softgel label amount; exact oral dose not given in the abstract
16881679 delivered oregano extract via a fortified juice vehicle rather than a standalone capsule, with dose expressed as phenolic-compound content rather than a whole-extract amount

36609950's oregano evidence comes from a network meta-analysis in a clinical chronic-rhinosinusitis population with low-certainty GRADE evidence, and the specific oregano preparation/dose is not stated in the abstract

excluded_pmids.reason: Meta-analysis pools 12 different Mediterranean-diet herbs/spices on glycemic control in T2DM; the abstract names cinnamon, turmeric, ginger, black cumin, and saffron as the herbs with significant fasting-glucose reductions, and does not separately state an oregano-specific effect size
Tests a 13-spice blend (including oregano) on postprandial cytokines; a combination product, not an isolated oregano exposure

Sensory/psychophysical study of carvacrol (an oregano constituent) and eugenol on tongue warmth/heat-pain perception; not a health outcome oregano is marketed for, and tests an isolated compound rather than an oregano supplement
Systematic review of medicinal plants (including Origanum vulgare) for infectious disease in poultry; animal/veterinary, not human
Systematic review of medicinal plants for GI/respiratory disease in calves and piglets; animal/veterinary, not human
Sustainability/land-footprint meta-analysis of essential oil biopesticide production; agricultural/environmental study, not a human health outcome
Review of bioactive compounds (quercetin, kaempferol, rosmarinic acid, etc.) for type 2 diabetes; oregano is not among the compounds or sources discussed
Insecticidal/repellent activity of plant powders (including Origanum vulgare) against stored-grain weevils; agricultural pest control, not a human health outcome

Systematic review of dietary supplements for military physical performance and recovery; oregano is not among the reviewed supplement categories (protein, beta-alanine, creatine, probiotics, HMB) named in the abstract
